title: Three things restore (Berakhot 57b)
hookLine: a sound, a sight and a smell restore a person's spirit
tomorrow: a sold-out crowd: what blessing fits a sea of faces?

lines: A WINDOW, A CUP OF TEA.
A SOUND, A SIGHT, A SMELL.
cards: After a long day, some people put on one particular song before they even take off their shoes. Some open a window and just look. Some make tea mostly for the smell.
So what three things bring a worn-out person back to themselves? The Talmud has a short list, and you've probably already been using it: a sound, a sight, and a smell.

teach.h: A SOUND, A SIGHT, A SMELL.
teach.b: Here's the line, in plain words: three things restore a person's mind: a sound, a sight, and a smell.
The Hebrew says they bring back a person's da'at, their mind, their settledness. It's the picture of someone who has been scattered and is returned to themselves. Notice what the Talmud doesn't do.
It doesn't say which sound, which sight, which smell.
No approved playlist. It trusts each person to know theirs. Your sound might be rain on a car roof.

Someone else's is a grandmother humming in the kitchen. And look where the list sits: inside a tractate about blessings, the book that teaches stopping to bless a good smell, a place, a piece of bread.

teach.h: THE SENSES ARE A WAY BACK.
teach.b: The senses here aren't distractions from the spiritual life. They're one of the ways back into it. The soul enjoys scent, the page said a few days ago.
Now the sages add hearing and seeing, and say all three can put a scattered person back together. Here's the part worth telling someone tonight: the Talmud's cure for a frayed mind is not a lecture.
It's three senses, and a few quiet minutes.

how: The Talmud lists a sound, a sight and a smell as what restores a person's mind; Jewish practice already blesses many of these moments, from fragrant spices to the sight of the sea.

o: three prayers said each day to restore the soul
three good deeds that make up for one wrong
a sound, a sight and a smell bring a scattered mind back

games.q: the list and its meaning — tap the pairs.
p: a sound, a sight, a smell
a way back, not a distraction

s: the Talmud names the exact sound, sight and smell that restore you
it gives only the three senses and trusts each person to know theirs.
this list sits inside the tractate about blessings
Berakhot 57b, in the book that blesses bread, places and scent.
Jewish tradition treats the senses as a distraction from prayer
here the sages say a sound, a sight and a smell bring a person back.

games.q: your dad comes home from a brutal shift and snaps at everyone. your sister wants to sit him down right away and talk it through. what does Berakhot 57b suggest first?
o: talk it through now, while it's fresh, so nothing gets buried.
a sound, a sight or a smell first: his music, the porch, the soup.
leave him alone all night; a scattered mind has to fix itself.
games.why: three things restore a person's mind: a sound, a sight and a smell. the talk can come after he's back to himself.

practice: Spend this time on one of each. First listen for one sound and stay with it. Then rest your eyes on one thing you like looking at.
Last, find one smell, even your own sleeve or a cup, and breathe it in.

wordCard.voice: Three things restore: a sound, a sight and a smell, the Talmud's short list for bringing a scattered mind home.

orig.note: Hebrew: they restore his mind; 'three things restore a person's mind.'

carryVoice: For when you're frayed: three things restore, and none of them needs a lecture. Thirty-six, settled.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 57b (three things restore a person's mind: a sound, a sight and a smell)
